title: Thiacalix[4]arene-Sandwiched Sandglass-like Ln9 Clusters (Ln = Tb and Eu): Insights into the Selective Luminescence Quenching Properties by p-Nitrobenzene Derivatives

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of H4TC4A (80 mg, 0.11 mmol) and Tb(CH3COO)3·6H2O (200 mg, 0.55 mmol) in CH3OH (3 mL), DMF (7 mL), and H2O (1 mL) was sealed in a 25 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, heated at 130 °C for 72 h, and cooled to room temperature at 4 °C h−1. The mixture was filtered and the colorless filtrate was allowed to stand at room temperature; single crystals appeared after about 3 days. Crystals were isolated by filtration, washed with CH3OH/DMF/H2O (3:7:1 v/v/v), and dried in vacuum at 80 °C for 6 h.

properties.summary: Solid-state Tb9 shows ligand-sensitized Tb(III) 5D4→7FJ (J=6–3) emission with strongest band at 547 nm (λex 348 nm) and QY 17.6% (17.63% in the conclusions). In methanol, QY reaches 59.2% (59.19%) at 2×10−5 mol/L (λex 318 nm), with concentration-dependent AIE then aggregation-caused quenching. Green emission is selectively quenched by p-nitrobenzene derivatives (quenching ~20% for R=CH3COO to ~90% for R=COOH); Stern–Volmer titration of 1,4-DNB, 4-NAN, 4-NP, 4-NA, and 4-NBA was used as a sensory platform.

Filtrate crystallization at room temperature (~3 days), wash with CH3OH/DMF/H2O (3:7:1 v/v/v), vacuum dry at 80 °C for 6 h.

properties.summary: Solid-state photoluminescence of isostructural Eu9 was examined analogously to Tb9, but efficient TC4A-to-Eu energy transfer was not observed (Figure S7), in contrast to Tb9.
